node.name: Renew Office Yoga Fall Series - Tuesdays
node.descriptionText:
Take a break for Renew Office Yoga to boost happiness, create calm, sharpen focus, and increase energy! Each 30-minute Zoom session in this series includes breath awareness techniques, gentle stretches, seated and standing yoga postures. Learn simple yet effective practices to renew vitality, build strength and flexibility, and restore balance.
 
These unique sessions are sponsored by Being Well at Yale and the Working Women’s Network and led by Danielle Casioppo, MS, NBC-HWC, Education Specialist and certified yoga instructor with Being Well at Yale. 
 
This series is open to all Yale employees who wish to participate and is suitable for beginners, no experience required.

node.name: Daily Worship at Marquand Chapel
node.descriptionText:
Join us at 11:30am in Marquand Chapel for our daily worship.

Worship in Marquand often draws on a wide variety of inherited Christian traditions, with the worship of many denominations being represented. Beyond that, though, we also pay attention to the rising number of people in Western society who have a lively interest in spirituality but feel no connection to traditional forms of church and worship. So Marquand is also actively engaged in original, creative, and experimental forms of worship, both for committed Christians and for those exploring the faith.

node.name: Can a Yale Startup Change the Way America Buys Wood?
node.descriptionText:
How do you turn an environmental ambition into a business—and what can you learn along the way?

Join CBEY and Tsai CITY for a lunch conversation with Ben Christensen ’20 MEM, co-founder and CEO of Cambium, a company using technology to connect the wood industry and expand access to sustainable wood products.

Ben will reflect on his journey from Yale to building and growing Cambium, sharing the experiences, decisions, and challenges that have shaped his path.

node.name: Faculty Fellows Event: Facilitating Complex Conversations in the Classroom
node.foodDetails: Please let us know of any dietary requirements.
node.descriptionText:
As instructors, how do we help students navigate controversial topics and discussions, especially those deeply intertwined with their lived experiences and identities? How do we know when to lean into hard conversations with our students? Please join us for a discussion about teaching across the disciplines with Tisa Wenger (Professor of American Religious History, Yale Divinity School, American Studies, History, and Religious Studies) and Pádraig Ó Tuama, (Professor in the Practice of Spirituality, Yale Divinity School). Ó Tuama, a noted conflict mediator and poet-theologian, will bring his experience as the leader of Corrymeela (Ireland’s oldest peace and reconciliation community) to bear on a conversation about the unevenly distributed risks and rewards of teaching in 2026. 

Participants will have the chance to hear from Professors Wenger and Ó Tuama about their classrooms, as well as the opportunity to share their own questions and insights with the speakers and each other.

node.name: Dissertation Writing as Practice Series (Session 5): 12/1
node.descriptionText:
This series provides dissertation writers with the structure, resources, and creative outlets to design and maintain a sustainable approach to writing. We will explore effective practices for pacing your dissertation writing while helping you overcome common writing blocks and find balance in your writing life. During each weekly live workshop session, we will engage with a relevant theme, discuss your writing practice and progress, and complete low-stakes reflective and creative activities to build your writing momentum. Invigorated by poetry, art, and other creative inspirations, and supported through discussion boards and supplementary resources, we will help you craft a writing practice to help you maintain, and even enjoy, a PhD writing life. 

As part of the resources offered in this series, students will receive access to tutorials on how to try Scrivener, a software program for organizing writing and brainstorming. Students who attend at least four of the six sessions will receive a free, lifetime Scrivener license.

The weekly session themes are:  

1. Time Management and Dissertation Planning (10/27)
2. Crafting a Holistic Dissertation Writing Practice (11/3)
3. Working through Distractions and Procrastination (11/10)
4. Writing through Imposter Stress (11/17)
5. Hanging up on Perfectionism and Demoralization (12/1)
6. Assessing Process & Progress + Long-View Spring Semester Planning (12/8)

Intended Audience:  ABD PhD students from all disciplines who have begun writing their dissertation.

node.name: Small Structures, Big Impact: When Our Immune System goes Local
node.descriptionText:
Speaker: Clémence Riffard, Immunobiology, YSM

Our immune system is remarkably good at detecting threats and organizing a response to protect our body. The spleen and lymph nodes (our secondary lymphoid organs) act as gathering points where immune cells can recognize threats and coordinate their defense. 
But what happens when an organ or tissue is threatened locally? Can the immune system build its own defense hubs exactly where they are needed?
This is the role of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS). These organized clusters of immune cells form in tissues during inflammation, and provide local environments where the immune defense can be orchestrated.
In this course, we will take a closer look at these intermediate structures: from the discoveries that brought them to light, to the mechanisms that drive their formation and function in the body. Ultimately, we will ask what these structures mean for many patients and whether understanding them could help us better prevent or treat various diseases.
